files.title: Journal — per-iteration handover
files.text:
# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — reuse prior-run measured champion (0.525 on these 40) + bounded fixes for its 7 regressions and 9 more failures
- Changes I made:
  - BASE: prompt.md + task_template.md = prior run's accepted cand_0001 (reused_seed_run), verbatim.
  - task_template Phase 2 snippet: read from `src` (data_only) and write to `wb`; convert leftover `=` cells in the target to cached values (clusters 1 and 6: 52541, 45707, 57354, 183-8).
  - task_template HOW TO WORK + Phase 3: only the first block runs; no invented output; no identical resend (print repr/type diagnostics instead) (cluster 2: 50811, 52541, 486-17, 12307, 203-15).
  - task_template CONTRACT 5: deleting whole rows/cols uses delete_rows/delete_cols, which shifts content (cluster 5: 28-7).
  - prompt.md §6 Excel semantics: case-insensitive matching, real today, TEXT codes / instruction example beats neighbours, blank only on a miss (9111, 534-26, 11276, 9391).
  - prompt.md §7 workbook-derived names and shape: header map, header = value kind, exact strings, finished-value shape, merged headers, membership filters, keyword categories, row ref stays key (50811, 188-39, 1925, 203-15, 279-23, 59160, 12307, 524-31, 45944).
- Expected effect + safety:
  - Keep the base's +12 fixes, and win back some of the 7 protected regressions.
  - Every new rule is conditional on its trigger. Trigger scans: delete → 6 val tasks (3 already use delete_*); today → 534-26 only; lookup-case → 11 tasks, framed as matching only, so written values are unchanged.
  - The snippet change is a bug fix.
- Building on prior RESULTS: the prior run's 0002–0005 were all rejected. I did NOT add mandatory steps, prune, add a blanket openpyxl rule, or an anti-relitigation clause.
- Refuted hypotheses: (from prior run) more mandatory phases; pruning the champion.
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: 38074, 59358 and others with no clear general cause; the 45944/12307 fixes are medium confidence.
- Plateau signal: n/a (iteration 1).
- Focus next iteration: read this RESULT's broke/fixed. If a §6/§7 rule broke a protected task, drop just that bullet. If resend loops persist, tighten the Phase 3 stop rule.

> **RESULT (framework, measured):** ACCEPTED (new champion) · val=0.700 Δ=+0.300 · fixed={11276, 12307, 290-1, 304-35, 38074, 409-45, 41978, 45707, 469-9, 50682, 524-31, 535-20, 56921, 58687, 59160, 59358} · broke={188-39, 374-31, 51680, 547-43} · unresolved={—} (moved less than 2·SE of its own measurement — NOT evidence the edit touched those tasks; do not redesign on them).

# META-INSIGHTS — about the optimization PROCESS itself (this run)

Not about the capability — about HOW this run is searching for it: which strategies/edit classes/algorithms are helping vs stalling, and what to try next iteration. Update at the end of the run at minimum; sooner if a plateau or a clear strategy shift is worth recording now. Structure each addition as:

    ## Iteration <id> (or 'run so far')
    - Strategy tried, and whether it moved val (cite LEDGER rows):
    - Plateau/stall signal, if any, and the lever switched to:
    - What to try next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001
- Strategy tried: the local trajectories had no traces, so I used the prior run's FINAL test traces on the SAME 40 val tasks to measure its champion (0.525, +12/−7 vs seed). I then reused it as the base and spent the iteration on bounded fixes for its exact regressions. Cheaper and better-grounded than writing from an empty prompt. Val movement: pending RESULT.
- Stall signal: the prior run plateaued after one accept: four rejects, all "add a mandatory step / prune". The lever I switched to is conditional knowledge bullets plus fixing the point-of-use snippet.
- What to try next: if this lands, attribute broke/fixed per bullet and remove the losers one at a time. If resend loops persist, consider a task_template-level change to the stop protocol rather than more prose.

# FRAMEWORK-IMPROVEMENTS — suggestions for cap-evolve itself (cross-run)

NOT about this capability or this run's result — about what cap-evolve the FRAMEWORK should change so FUTURE runs (any capability, any project) go better: a confusing prompt section, a missing tool, a file you wished existed, a gate that felt wrong. Optional most iterations; add an entry whenever something about the framework itself (not the task) got in your way or surprised you.

- Local `trajectories/` and `rollouts/val` for the seed held only score rows, no traces. The optimizer had to dig into a sibling run's rollouts/test. Ship seed traces with the work dir.
- Grader feedback text is sometimes misleading: 45944 is reported as int-vs-bool and 188-39 as str-vs-float, while the real issue is the wrong value or source column. Report the expected/actual repr instead.
- The adapter's verify budget resets on every re-save, so an identical resubmission loops to MAX_TURNS. A harness-side "identical block → end task" detector would save turns and noise.

files.name: PROCESS.md
files.title: Process — best candidate (cand_0001)
files.text:
# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

**Strategy.** The capability started EMPTY (seed = no system prompt, val 0.400). The local
trajectories carry no traces, so I used the FINAL test traces of the prior run's champion
(`reused_seed_run/run_suite/candidates/cand_0001`) on these same 40 val tasks. Measured there:
0.525 vs the seed's 0.400. It fixes 12 tasks and breaks 7, and all 7 are on our protected list.
So I took that champion as the BASE (copied verbatim) and added BOUNDED, condition-scoped rules:
first for each of the 7 regressions, then for the remaining failures I could diagnose from
init/golden diffs. I added NO new mandatory phases or steps, because the prior run rejected those
four times (cand_0002–0005: extra Phase-1/3 steps, pruning, blanket "always openpyxl",
anti-relitigation).

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Computed from a non-data_only workbook (formula strings read as values) | 52541*, 45707, 57354 | Base Phase-2 snippet loads `wb` without data_only and the model computes from it, so formula cells read as `"=..."`, lookups/comparisons fail, and it loops on identical code | BEHAVIORAL (snippet bug) | fix the point-of-use snippet |
| 2 | Identical resend / invented stdout | 50811*, 52541*, 45707 (loops); 486-17*, 12307, 203-15 (fake output) | Re-saves reset the verify budget, so a resend runs to the turn cap; the model writes "expected output" or several blocks | BEHAVIORAL | turn-protocol rule + "print diagnostics instead of resend" |
| 3 | Excel-semantics mismatches | 9111* (case-insensitive lookup), 534-26* (today), 11276 (TEXT codes), 9391 (blank only on miss) | Python semantics differ from Excel's | KNOWLEDGE | §6 rules |
| 4 | Workbook-derived labels / shape | 50811* (cols by header), 188-39* (header = value kind), 1925 + 203-15 (exact strings), 279-23 (finished-value shape), 59160 (merged headers), 12307 (membership filter), 524-31 (keyword categories), 45944 (row ref stays key) | Model retypes or guesses instead of reading the sheet | KNOWLEDGE | §7 rules |
| 5 | Deletion done as blanking | 28-7* | CONTRACT 3/4 "preserve" pushes the model to blank in place instead of `delete_rows` | CONTRACT (conflict) | CONTRACT exception 5 |
| 6 | Pre-existing formula left in target | 183-8 | An untouched formula cell in answer_position reads empty under hard_no_recalc | CONTRACT | Phase-2 snippet converts leftover formulas |

`*` = protected task (seed passes, base champion failed it). The 7 regressions are 28-7, 52541,
534-26, 9111, 50811, 188-39, 486-17.

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| base | reuse measured champion | prompt.md + task_template.md | copy of prior-run cand_0001 (0.525 on these 40) | it breaks 7 protected tasks; edits R1–R7 target exactly those |
| 1 (+6) | snippet fix | task_template.md Phase 2 | read from `src` (data_only), write to `wb`; convert leftover `=` cells in the target to `ss` cached values; one-line "if an input prints `=...` you read the wrong workbook" | pure bug fix; a correct reader behaves the same |
| 2 | behavioral | task_template.md HOW TO WORK + Phase 3 | only the first block runs, never write expected output; don't resend an identical block, stop or print repr/type of the failing condition's inputs | only affects replies that would be identical/fake |
| 5 | contract | task_template.md CONTRACT 5 | delete whole rows/cols → `delete_rows`/`delete_cols` bottom-up; "delete the values" excluded | triggers 28-7, 374-31, 534-26, 535-20, 409-45 (whole rows/cols); 374-31/534-26/535-20 already use delete_* |
| 3 | knowledge | prompt.md §6 | case-insensitive matching (match only, written value unchanged); today = `datetime.today()`; TEXT format codes + instruction example beats neighbours + apply to whole range; blank-on-miss only on misses | lookup rule touches 11 val tasks; framed as how to *match*, so written values are unchanged |
| 4 | knowledge | prompt.md §7 | columns by header map; header = value kind; text copied from workbook; match finished-value shape (example drops brackets: `(tig) …` → `tig`); merged headers carry; every block has a role / membership filter; keyword "longest wins + print unmatched"; row ref stays key | each is conditional on its trigger |

## Verify-the-fix (the trace each change targets → what it now does on those exact inputs)
- 52541/45707/57354: the trace computed on `wb` (formula strings) and looped. The snippet now names
  `ss` as the read source and prints `was:` from `ss`, and a stray `=` input is explicitly flagged.
- 183-8: the answer_position held a formula the model did not touch → it read empty. The snippet
  loop now rewrites any remaining `=` cell in the target to its cached value before save.
- 28-7: the final code blanked the matching rows. CONTRACT 5 now requires `delete_rows` (shift
  up); the instruction says "delete all rows", so it triggers. 304-35 ("delete the values") does not.
- 534-26: the model took "current month" from the latest date in the data. Golden keeps columns
  ≥ 2020-12 in the Result sheet, so the anchor is a fixed real date, not the data max (2022-06).
  §6 says today = `datetime.today()`.
- 9111: "EVA" vs "Eva" mismatched under Python `==`. §6 normalises keys for matching only.
- 11276: init F3 holds `=TEXT(F4,"DD")`, neighbours hand-typed `TU, W, TH…`, golden `Wed, Thu, Fri…`.
  §6 gives `ddd`=Mon and says the instruction example ("Mon, Wed") beats neighbours, applied to the
  whole row.
- 279-23: the model kept the parentheses (`(tig)`). Golden and the finished cells B17+ read `tig`.
  The §7 example is exactly that shape (taken from the general pattern, not hardcoded to the cell).
- 50811/188-39/1925/203-15/59160/12307/524-31/9391/45944: §7/§6 rules as listed. Diagnosed by
  subagents from the traces plus the golden diff. Medium confidence for 45944 and 12307.
- Placeholder safety: ran `str.format` on the template (comment stripped AND raw) with all 7
  keys → OK. Parsed field set = exactly the 6 required + `max_turns`. The adapter does not
  `.format()` prompt.md (checked adapter.py:1359/1378), so braces in §7 are safe.

## Process & features used
- Subagents: 3 parallel read-only general-purpose agents ("Diagnose regressions group A",
  "Diagnose failures group B1", "B2"). They traced the 7 regressions and the remaining failures
  against init/golden diffs. Their claims were spot-checked by me (534-26, 11276, 9111, 279-23 re-read).
- Prior iterations: RUNMAP is empty and there is no prior_iterations/ (iteration 1). Instead I read the reused
  seed run's JOURNAL / history / rejected record. Learned: cand_0001 accepted; 0002–0005 rejected for
  adding mandatory steps, pruning, a blanket openpyxl rule, and an anti-relitigation clause. None of these
  are re-proposed.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- §1(a) literal-not-formula; §1(b) the date-serial ban; §2 worked-example rule; §4 data_only save trap;
  the Phase-1b calibration block (it fixed tasks in the prior run).
- The Phase-2 `src`/`wb` split (read data_only, write non-data_only).

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)
- No new mandatory phase/step and no pruning (refuted in the prior run, cand_0002–0005).
- Remaining failures without a clear general root cause from the diff (e.g. 38074, 59358). I did
  not hardcode them.
- No harness-level resend detector: that would be a framework change, so it is logged in FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.

# Optimize the capability — ship several REAL, SAFE, VERIFIED prompt fixes this iteration

{{TARGET_READER}}

{{FOCUS_SUMMARY}}

{{EMPTY_SEED}}

GOAL: raise the eval score as much as you can THIS iteration, then STOP (the harness
re-scores you — don't run evaluation yourself). The capability under optimization is
PROSE: the agent's prompt / skill text. There are no tool implementations to edit here.

Make **AS MANY real fixes as you can this iteration — solve many issues across many
trajectories, not just the biggest one.** A timid one- or two-edit iteration is an
under-used iteration: diagnose EVERY failure cluster in `./trajectories/` and ship a fix
for each one that passes the three tests below. Breadth is the goal — the more distinct
failing clusters you fix in this ONE candidate, the larger the gain.

The ONLY brake on breadth is regression: every edit must pass all three tests, because a
single speculative edit that breaks a passing task can sink an iteration of good work (it
did in prior runs). So the discipline is "many fixes, each one real and safe" — NOT "few
fixes". Do not stop at the first cluster; work through them all.

## WHAT YOU MAY EDIT — and the two ways iterations get wasted here
Edit ONLY the capability files listed in `{{CAP_BRIEF}}` below (the prompt / skill text in
this working directory). Everything else you can see is READ-ONLY CONTEXT.

**You may NOT edit the adapter, the harness, the scorer, the benchmark, or the
environment** — not to make a task pass, not to fix a broken mount or a missing binary,
not "just to unblock the run". Those files are how your score is MEASURED; changing them
does not improve the capability, and a gain obtained that way is not a result. An
iteration that edits infrastructure has produced NOTHING measurable, however green the
number looks. **If the traces show an ENVIRONMENT fault** (permission denied, missing
binary, gateway/network error, timeout, container failure — the same error on nearly every
task, unrelated to the task's content), then the correct and complete action is:
1. do NOT edit the prompt to work around it (a prose workaround for a broken environment
   is a speculative edit that fails the REAL test — the prompt is not the defect), and
2. state the diagnosis in `PROCESS.md` and `JOURNAL.md` precisely — the exact error, how
   many tasks it hit, and what a human must fix — then STOP. Handing back an accurate
   "the environment is broken, here is the evidence" is a SUCCESSFUL iteration.

**The other way iterations get wasted: another prose rule for a behavior the agent already
knows.** When the agent has the rule and skips it anyway, adding a second sentence saying
the same thing changes nothing — you must change the STRUCTURE that makes it skippable
(see the levers below): make the step unavoidable and ordered, make the contract explicit,
or give a worked example it can pattern-match. Prose is for genuine KNOWLEDGE gaps (a
fact / format / criterion the agent cannot derive) and for STRUCTURE that changes what the
agent does — not for repetition or emphasis.

## The THREE TESTS every change must pass (this is the whole game)
Before you keep any edit, confirm all three. Drop any edit that fails even one.
1. **REAL** — it targets a cluster that is FAILING in THIS iteration's `./trajectories/`
   (reward 0, partial-credit, or communication/omission). Never edit for a hypothetical
   problem, and never edit on account of a task whose failure is an environment fault.
2. **SAFE (bounded blast radius)** — the real regression question is *behavioral*:
   **would this edit change what the agent DOES on ANY currently-passing task?** Two
   blast-radius classes:
   - **BOUNDED** — an ADDITIVE rule that applies only under a stated condition present in
     the failing cases, or a clarification of an output contract the passing tasks already
     satisfy. This is the SAFE default — prefer it.
   - **UNBOUNDED** — any edit to a GLOBAL decision/permission/refusal rule, or a …[+13631 chars truncated]
